title: Return from Europe, Cincinnati hotel work and band members
summary: After Germany and London the band returns, with a rough boat crossing, then works the Sinton Hotel in Cincinnati; he lists substitute players.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Then we went back to Denmark and we left from there and went to Baden-Baden, Germany for a week for a TV show. So, naturally, it was more of a cabaret scene. And we rehearsed that whole week. And when we finished there, we left and went back to London. And that was when, well, everything was over with. Then the boys got ready to come on. Well, Joe Rovershow, Howard, Jim, Miss Tate, George, they all left by plane. Well, Jack and I came back by boat. And that was when we run into that 80-mile gale. And I'm telling you, it was really rough. Well, when we landed in New York, it had been snowing there, too. And that's where I started to feel my pains. So, we came on back home. Then they walked us back in Ohio again, in Cincinnati. Well, at the Sinton Hotel. The Sinton, S-I-N-T-O-N, Sinton Hotel. Well, we went to work there for a couple of months, I believe. Well, we stayed in the hotel right where we was playing. So, we got through there. We came on back to New Orleans. And the Sheraton Gibson warned us. Well, we went on back there. What was that? That was right around the corner from where the Sinton was on, uh...

On 6th Street or 5th Street. That was in Cincinnati. Uh, we played there about six weeks or eight weeks. That was a whole band? Yeah, that was a whole band. We had, uh... We had on trumpet. Howard. Yes, Howard was on trumpet. And then we had, uh, this is a crippled trombone player there. Because Jim had taken the sick and they got him to work in his place. Oh, he plays with... He was playing with Bob Bob, Brandon, all the time.
Oh, I know what you mean by Derek, or Bob, Frog.
